responsibility: This module is GCC’s interprocedural analysis and callgraph subsystem centered on the global symbol table, callgraph, and IPA passes that reason across whole functions rather than within a single GIMPLE body. Its core cgraph/symtab files define and maintain function/variable nodes, call and reference edges, cloning, thunks, aliases, unit finalization, and rebuilding of graph connectivity from GIMPLE, while shared IPA infrastructure files provide propagation summaries, predicates, SCC/order utilities, and function/call cost models used by many passes. On top of that substrate, the ipa-* families implement the major whole-program analyses and transformations that consume and update the graph: inlining and function summaries, constant propagation and specialization, devirtualization and polymorphic-call reasoning, profile propagation, pure/const and mod/ref side-effect analysis, static-reference tracking, identical code folding, parameter and aggregate signature rewriting, partial splitting, visibility/COMDAT/locality handling, and specialized interprocedural support such as CHKP, HSA, and strub. In short, this module owns the middle-end’s whole-program callgraph-driven optimization framework and the symbol-level bookkeeping that lets GCC analyze, clone, redirect, merge, and prepare functions and variables before final code generation or LTO partitioning.
